slots.hypothesis: dw(Close) is a misnamed intraday realized variance: its denominator is not demeaned. The 3 M3 heads (+1.56/+1.44/+0.67, sign -1) get their score from convexity before the EMA. long_neutral z-ranks the smoothed signal before it projects out the controls (steer.py:430), so convexity can only act through the EMA, and EMA(dw^4) is roughly the peak intraday variance of the last month or two. Read this way, the family measures peak and vol-of-vol beyond the 20-day mean-vol control. The E slot puts those 3 heads into the controls and grows 16 scale-free peripheries with no signedpower or pow_*: spike ratios, log-scale vol-of-vol and the coefficient of variation, two-scale variance ratios (1-minute vs 5-minute, and intraday vs daily), the time-of-day share of variance (first 30 minutes, last 30 minutes, morning), and the bipower/RV continuous share.

The shape of the intraday minute-return distribution above second order. None of the 594 scored candidates ever used it, and none of the controls covers it. 14 short single-axis seeds: realized kurtosis and skewness (daily, 5-day, 20-day, and a 5-minute-return version), relative signed jump variation sum(r|r|)/sum(r^2), max and min minute returns standardized by day_std, and left/right tail ES/VaR ratios. Sources: Amaya et al. 2011-12, Barndorff-Nielsen-Kinnebrock-Shephard 2008-08, Patton-Sheppard 2015-07, Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw 2011. PLAN revision 3 records day_kurt(Ret) as a head in another seed of the same environment; that one sentence is the only use of it, and it is disclosed.
